svg.text: How search works in Python vs Node
One index, two readers. Same ids, same order, same band -- and three places Node is a SUBSET on purpose.
a twin module -- both runtimes
PYTHON ONLY -- no Node twin
deliberate asymmetry, not a gap
neither runtime -- unbuilt
0 - ONE INDEX. THE COMMITTED BYTES ARE THE WHOLE CONTRACT.
.fux/index/*.jsonl shards + sources/dirs + formats.toml + tune.toml + output.toml + pii.toml + acquired/objects/
Statistics about documents, never the documents. Python writes every one of these files; both readers read these and nothing else.
No server, no model, no clock, no network on the query path in either runtime.
Python `fux` -- pip install fux-engine
32 094 lines. 20 verbs; Node implements 7 of them.
THE REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION: when the two disagree,
this one is right by definition.
Node `fux` -- npm i fux-engine, vendored to .fux/node/
7 read verbs: find ask answer explain graph path mcp.
The other 13 REFUSE BY NAME and say who owns them.
Zero dependencies, no build step. Answers a clone with no Python.
1 - THE SHARED QUERY PIPELINE: TEN TWINS, ONE PER MODULE, AT THE SAME RELATIVE PATH (x/y.mjs -> src/fux/x/y.py)
tokenize.py / tokenize.mjs
39 / 11 lines. The one place a query becomes terms.
stem.py / stem.mjs
204 / 172. Suffix rules, transcribed rule for rule.
analyzer.py / analyzer.mjs
124 / 81. Term hashes, order PRESERVED -- rank() sums in it.
expand.py / expand.mjs
--expand: the CALLER's words. Fux never invents a term.
scan.py / scan.mjs
THE DEFAULT PATH. Every shard line read as raw bytes; flen and
mtime by regex; a line is parsed only if it substring-matches a hash.
bm25f.py + rank.py / .mjs
guard -> BM25F -> multipliers -> sort. Scoring lives here in both,
never in the candidate generator, so the two cannot drift.
fuse.py / fuse.mjs
-q -> reciprocal rank fusion.
rerank.py / rerank.mjs
Proximity rerank -- OFF unless rerank_weight > 0.
headings.py / headings.mjs
Section paths for the cited lines.
confidence.py / confidence.mjs
The band: grounded | weak | partial | none. Plus answerable, missing.
one ranked, banded list -- identical in both runtimes
ingest/pii.py (618 lines)
The redaction engine runs at INGEST, so
both readers inherit redacted bytes.
Python owns the rules, the luhn and
verhoeff validators, and PII_EXEMPT.
Node's gate is a STAT, not a parse.
.fux/pii.toml must exist or every verb
refuses. There is no Node twin of
PII_EXEMPT and none is needed: all four
exempt verbs are write verbs here.
derive/accel.py (520 lines)
THE ACCELERATOR, and it has no Node twin.
.fux/runtime/ postings, rarest-first, exact
theta, block-max bound, skip test. Taken only
on --fast AND a fresh stamp; else it falls
through to the scan -- never a wrong answer.
measured: 4.2 s scan -> 27.2 ms warm p95
query/provenance.py (771 lines)
--why, --receipt, --journal, and the whole
verify verdict set (reproduced | drifted |
unverifiable). NO NODE TWIN AT ALL.
A stated absence (W-107 R6) -- these four
surfaces are uncovered by the arm, openly.
Node ALWAYS scans.
There is no accelerator and no --fast/--scan
flag to choose one. Python's MCP reports
ranked_by: "accelerator" on a fresh build;
Node reports "scan".
Same documents, same order -- the LABEL is the
only difference; the arm excludes it BY NAME.
Node reads tune.toml + output.toml.
Closed 2026-09-12. Before it, a tuned repo
ranked DIFFERENTLY in the two readers with
nothing saying so: 90 of 174 discordant.
After: 0 of 199. --no-tune is a two-runtime
flag now, or it is not the switch it claims.
2 - THREE PYTHON SEMANTICS THE NODE READER REIMPLEMENTS -- each one is a correctness fix, not a nicety
round(x, 9) is half-EVEN
on the exact binary value. toFixed(9)
is half-UP and fails exactly on ties --
and a tie resolved the other way is a
DIFFERENT ORDER.
repr(float) exponent thresholds
Python switches at e < -4 or e >= 16;
JS at -6 / 21. Both shortest-round-trip,
so only the printed layout differs.
cmpCodePoints on every id
Python compares by CODE POINT, JS by
UTF-16 code UNIT. The sort key ends in id,
so one emoji reorders results: 30 of 324
ordered pairs disagreed, measured.
Three Node files therefore have NO Python twin, and the exemption list is short on purpose -- it is exactly where divergence risk concentrates:
hash/blake2b.mjs (hashlib cannot be reached from node:crypto) | compat/pyfloat.mjs | config/toml.mjs (CPython tomllib IS the twin, and it is stdlib).
3 - THE REFER PLANE (`fux answer`) -- where the two readers genuinely part company
Shared twins -- ranking has already chosen the documents before any of this runs, so nothing here changes WHICH document is cited, only which passage:
chunk.py / .mjs
556/263 lines
rescore.py / .mjs
190/106 lines
assemble.py / .mjs
205/88 lines
source.py / .mjs
172/45 lines
freshness.py / .mjs
252/51 lines
IN PYTHON ONLY
decode/ -- 17 built-in decoders + .fux/decoders/*.py
pdf, image, html, mail, json, xlsx, docx ... A consumer decoder is
arbitrary Python; there can be no Node twin of it, ever.
refer/arc.py -- the (loc, sha) ARC content cache
refer/fetchcache.py -- the TTL url cache
ingest fetchers -- http.py, the signed-in-Chrome cdp.py, refusals.toml
Node's decode/ is TWO files: a registry that answers one question,
and markdown.mjs. Nothing else, and nothing planned.
WHAT NODE DOES INSTEAD
Node has NO TRANSPORT. Not off by default -- there is no
fetcher seam and nothing to inject one through.
file: reads the working tree (your own checkout is not a fetch).
url: reads .fux/acquired/, else falls back to source: "index".
A document that needs a DECODER is DECLINED, not guessed at.
The question asked is never "does a decoder claim this extension?"
but "is this ALREADY TEXT?" -- which formats.toml's include list
answers in committed bytes both runtimes read. Under-claiming is the
only safe direction: a wrong citation vs the next candidate.
So the url: freshness verdict set is ASYMMETRIC, deliberately
verdict
PYTHON
NODE
why
current / stale
file: and url:
file: ONLY
Node cannot look at a URL
as-ingested
yes
yes
the acquired blob is local
unverified
yes
yes
we did not look
cached
yes
NEVER
a TTL fetch cache requires fetching
Node reporting `current` for a URL it never
checked would make the claim-strength vocabulary
mean different things in two runtimes -- the one
thing SR-URL-FRESHNESS exists to prevent.
A DECISION. NOT A GAP.
4 - THE THIRD ASYMMETRY: THE DERIVED GRAPH PLANE -- and here it is PYTHON that refuses
Python: graph/plane.py::load
Reads the derived .fux/runtime/graph.json and REFUSES
when it is absent or stale. explain / graph / path
all need a fresh `fux build`.
Node: graph/plane.mjs
Rebuilds the same plane IN MEMORY from the committed
records and answers either way. .fux/runtime/ is gitignored
and Python-written -- requiring it would refuse where Node is the only reader.
It follows that explain / graph / path cannot be COMPARED on a corpus with no fresh build, and node_arm.py::graph_lane_ready says so out loud rather than skipping quietly.
5 - WHAT HOLDS THEM EQUAL -- a second implementation is a second thing to keep true
The differential arm, SIX surfaces since 2026-09-12 -- it covered ONE before, and all three defects found that day lived on a surface it did not reach
1 find 2 ask 3 explain / graph / path, whole parsed payloads 4 the MCP server, a real stdio session 5 fux.api vs node/src/index.mjs 6 the BUNDLE vs the module tree
tests/test_node_twins.py maps every .mjs to its .py and fails when a Python twin changes and its .mjs does not -- which the arm structurally cannot catch.
tests/test_node_config_parity.py asserts the key sets and the REFUSALS, because a drifted refusal never shows up as a finding, only as a crash on one side.
Tolerance: scores equal after round(9), the sort key's own resolution. ORDERING is byte-equal and has no tolerance -- a discordant top-5 fails the arm.
6 - IN NEITHER RUNTIME -- named so that absence is not mistaken for coverage
the vector plane
W-112, open. No embeddings anywhere
on either query path.
Node's latency
W-148 row 2. fux-benchmark is unbuilt, so
the number is stated as UNMEASURED.
verify --why --receipt
W-107 R6. No Node twin at all, so the
arm does not pretend to cover them --
a stated absence, not a gap.

Drawn from the code 2026-09-12; surface 6 and the bundle added the same day (W-149). Authority: records/0153_node-search.md (SR-NODE-SEARCH), decisions 1-16. Every difference not on this page is a defect.
